interactions.summary: The host asks Jiang to define Predictive History and explain how it works.
Jiang defines Predictive History as a falsifiable historical method: good models project the future, and prediction errors are what force model revision.
The host asks Jiang to apply the method to the coming midterm election and clarifies the short-time-horizon objection.
Jiang says short horizons are hard because there is not enough data and because current conditions are unstable enough that ordinary midterm assumptions may fail.
The host pivots to Jiang's Iran call and asks why he thought U.S. military intervention was inevitable when many analysts expected restraint.

claims.claim: Jiang says conventional history is flawed because it does not generate predictions that can test whether the model is right.
He defines Predictive History as building theories of history that let him forecast how the world will progress and then correcting the model when the forecasts fail.
Jiang says midterm predictions are hard on a one-year horizon because there is not enough information or data to support a stable forecast.
He argues the next midterm may not behave like previous midterms because current politics could include discrepancies, cheating, or cancellations that break the pattern.
claims.temporal_scope: Conditional near-term election diagnosis stated on 2025-07-23.

claims.claim: Jiang says current polling points to Democrats retaking the House and starting impeachment hearings against Trump, though he adds Trump likely has counterstrategies.

signature_moments.moment: History is only 'properly' done if it can project the future and survive contact with prediction.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's clean methodological test and the basis for why his channel treats forecasting as proof rather than entertainment.

signature_moments.moment: Prediction failure is not embarrassing noise but the mechanism for repairing the model.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I know how to remedy or alter my NFL models
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It frames Predictive History as iterative model correction instead of static punditry.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang refuses the midterm call because he thinks the system itself may mutate rather than repeat.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It shows that for Jiang the model sometimes blocks prediction when the regime conditions are too unstable.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's method of testing historical theories by whether they generate correct future predictions and by revising the model when they fail.
Jiang's requirement that some predictions need more elapsed history and more data before he considers them responsibly forecastable.

chronology_notes.note: On 2025-07-23 Jiang treats the next midterm as too near and too unstable for a clean forecast, even while sketching the poll-driven House scenario.

uncertainty_notes.note: ASR repeatedly renders Jiang's phrase as 'NFL model'; the surrounding logic indicates he means his general predictive model, so the semantic extraction stays at the methodological level.
